items.stem: After building an existing-ground surface, a designer notices sharp vertical spikes that do not match the terrain. What is the most likely cause and correct response?

options.text: Erroneous survey points; identify and exclude or correct the bad data, then rebuild the surface
options.rationale: Correct: spikes usually come from bad survey points, which should be found and cleaned before relying on the surface.

options.text: The surface is correct; terrain naturally has vertical spikes
options.rationale: Real ground does not produce sharp vertical spikes; these indicate data errors.

options.text: Delete the whole surface and never use survey data
options.rationale: Survey data is the correct basis; the fix is cleaning errant points, not abandoning it.

options.text: Increase the drawing scale to hide the spikes
options.rationale: Changing scale hides the symptom but leaves the faulty surface in use.

items.explanation: Correct: spikes usually come from bad survey points, which should be found and cleaned before relying on the surface.

items.stem: Which TWO behaviours follow from Civil 3D's dynamic object model? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Editing an alignment automatically updates the profiles and corridors that reference it
options.rationale: Correct: dependent objects update when the governing object changes.

options.text: A surface data reference lets several drawings share one surface source
options.rationale: Correct: data references share model objects dynamically across drawings.

options.text: Design objects are static once drawn and must be redrawn to change
options.rationale: The model is dynamic; objects update rather than being redrawn.

options.text: Quantities never change when the design changes
options.rationale: Quantities extracted from the model update as the design changes.

items.explanation: Correct: dependent objects update when the governing object changes.

items.stem: A designer copies alignment geometry as plain lines into a sheet file to speed up drafting. What design risk does this create?

options.text: The copied linework no longer updates when the design changes, so sheets can go stale
options.rationale: Correct: static copies break the dynamic link and drift out of sync with the model.

options.text: Nothing; static copies always stay current
options.rationale: Static copies do not update with the model.

options.text: The alignment is deleted from the source drawing
options.rationale: Copying does not delete the source alignment.

options.text: The corridor volumes become more accurate
options.rationale: Static linework has no effect on corridor volume accuracy.

items.explanation: Correct: static copies break the dynamic link and drift out of sync with the model.
